items.title: Euro futures rally off monthly lows as Fed rate expectations shift.
items.excerpt: Euro futures recently rebounded from new monthly lows near 1.1350 to close the session higher. The shift in momentum occurred as the dollar retreated in the broader market. Market participants are currently recalibrating their expectations for tomorrow's FOMC meeting, with the probability of a near-term rate hike dropping from nearly 40% to closer to 20%. The market focus is now shifting toward the September meeting. Meanwhile, CVOL data indicates that volatility remains elevated as market uncertainty persists. Additionally, speculators have continued to increase their net short positions, pushing them to the highest levels seen since February 2025.

items.title: Rates Spark: Hike temptation
items.excerpt: We don't call for a hike, but can see how it could happen. Kevin Warsh does not believe in forward guidance. He might also have a preference not to slavishly deliver the market discount. If so, and if Warsh is minded to hike (maybe he is), better to do it now rather than 'risk' it being fully discounted at a subsequent meeting. Where's the nouveaux Fed in that?

items.title: British Pound futures erased gains ahead of BOE decision.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming of KKM Financial analyzes the recent selling pressure in British Pound futures, which have traded lower in seven of the last eight sessions. After reaching a mid-month peak of 1.355, the pound has staircased lower to give back all of its July gains, returning to the 1.328 opening level. Deming explains that shifting market expectations surrounding Thursday's Bank of England rate decision are driving this downward momentum. While a recent rally in crude oil prices previously sparked thoughts of a potential rate hike, markets are now broadly expecting the central bank to hold rates steady. Traders continue to position defensively as short-term sentiment shifts ahead of the critical policy announcement.

items.title: Japanese Yen futures hit 40-year lows ahead of BOJ meeting.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners discusses the recent price action in September Japanese Yen futures as the market trades near a 40-year low. After falling 5.98% since the cycle high on May 6 and closing lower in 10 of the last 11 weeks, market participants remain alert to potential official action. Iaccino highlights recent comments from Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama signaling a readiness to intervene if necessary. He also looks ahead to the upcoming Bank of Japan policy meeting, where officials are widely expected to hold the benchmark rate at 1%, with economists largely projecting December as the most likely timing for the next rate hike.
